t:
The National Housing Act is amended—
    (1) in subsection (e) of section 202 (12 U.S.C. 1708(e))—
        (A) in paragraph (3)(B), by striking “section 202(e) of the National Housing Act” and inserting “this subsection”; and 
        (B) by redesignating such subsection as subsection (f);  
    (2) by striking paragraph (4) of section 203(s) (12 U.S.C. 1709(s)(4)) and inserting the following new paragraph:“(4) the Secretary of Agriculture;”; and 
    (3) by transferring subsection (s) of section 203 (as amended by paragraph (2) of this section) to section 202, inserting such subsection after subsection (d) of section 202, and redesignating such subsection as subsection (e).

fable.w: This section only makes technical and conforming amendments to the National Housing Act: it redesignates and moves subsections and substitutes a reference to the Secretary of Agriculture. The tempting reading is that the amended provisions might involve some process with outside parties, but the text here creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with non-federal actors, or right to sue. The only actor named is a federal official, who is inside the federal government.
fable.s: by transferring subsection (s) of section 203 (as amended by paragraph (2) of this section) to section 202

opus.w: The section only edits a cross-reference, redesignates subsections and moves a subsection within the National Housing Act. The only party it names is the Secretary of Agriculture, who is a federal official. Nothing in the text brings states, the public, experts or other outside parties into a federal decision, so it is not participation, even though restructuring the statute might look like it adds a new process.
opus.s: by striking paragraph (4) of section 203(s) (12 U.S.C. 1709(s)(4)) and inserting the following new paragraph:“(4) the Secretary of Agriculture;”
opus.b: This section is only a set of technical and conforming amendments to the National Housing Act. It changes a cross-reference, redesignates subsections, replaces one paragraph with "the Secretary of Agriculture" (a federal official), and moves subsection 203(s) into section 202. The tempting reading is that moving provisions around might create a new process. That fails because the text never sets up a comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outsiders, or a right to sue. The only party it names is a federal cabinet secretary, who is inside the federal government.

qwen_chat.w: This section consists of technical amendments to the National Housing Act, specifically redesignating subsections and inserting the Secretary of Agriculture into a list. The Secretary of Agriculture is a federal official, so any interaction with them is intra-governmental. There is no requirement for consultation with non-federal entities, public comment, or advisory boards involving outsiders.
qwen_chat.s: (2) by striking paragraph (4) of section 203(s) (12 U.S.C. 1709(s)(4)) and inserting the following new paragraph:“(4) the Secretary of Agriculture;”
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that adding the "Secretary of Agriculture" to a list implies consultation or coordination with an outside entity. However, the Secretary of Agriculture is a federal cabinet member, and thus inside the federal government. Furthermore, the text is purely technical, dealing with the reorganization and amendment of statutory references (redesignating subsections, striking and inserting text) rather than establishing a process for public or non-federal input.
